### Statitical Distribution Plots

```{python}

# Hisograms

# median daily average for a given year and county
sns.histplot(data=df, x=df["pm25_med_daily_avg"])
plt.show()

# Check for nomality with a QQ plot
fig = sm.qqplot(df["pm25_med_daily_avg"], fit=True, line="s")
plt.show()

# average daily maxiumum for a given year and county
sns.histplot(data=df, x=df["pm25_max_daily_avg"])
plt.show()
# Check for nomality with a QQ plot
fig = sm.qqplot(df["pm25_max_daily_avg"], fit=True, line="s")
plt.show()

# average daily average for a given year and county
sns.histplot(data=df, x=df["pm25_mean_daily_avg"])
plt.show()
# Check for nomality with a QQ plot
fig = sm.qqplot(df["pm25_mean_daily_avg"], fit=True, line="s")
plt.show()
```

The air quality data is right skewed meaning it is not normally distributed. 
We are using QQ-plots to evaluate normality rather than statitical tests like 
Shaprio-Wilks given the large sample size which can lead to false negatives on 
those tests. 


```{python}
# taking a closer look at high values

# select county-years with usually high average daily max values
df[df["pm25_max_daily_avg"] > 20]
```

All observations in our dataset with pm2.5 values greater than 20 are in Califonia
or Oregon. Many of those observations were in 2020.

### Geographic Distribution

```{python}
# load counties map data
geojson_path = data_dir / "county_fips_codes/geojson_counties_fips.json"

with open(geojson_path, "r") as f:
    counties_geojson = json.load(f)
```

#### Missingness Check
```{python}
# create map of counties for which we have data over time
def plot_county_coverage(df, table_name, value_col):
    map_df = df[["year", "county_id"]].dropna().drop_duplicates()
    years = sorted(map_df["year"].unique())
    frames = []

    # Compile chronological frame tracking data
    for year in years:
        df_year = map_df[map_df["year"] == year]
        frames.append(
            go.Frame(
                data=[
                    go.Choroplethmap(
                        locations=df_year["county_id"],
                        z=[1] * len(df_year),  
                    )
                ],
                name=str(int(year))
            )
        )

    if not frames:
        raise ValueError(f"No valid yearly data found for {table_name}")

    # Create base map matching geojson object
    initial_year_data = map_df[map_df["year"] == years[0]]
    fig = go.Figure(
        data=[
            go.Choroplethmap(
                geojson=counties_geojson, # References global object directly
                locations=initial_year_data["county_id"],
                z=[1] * len(initial_year_data),
                featureidkey="id",
                colorscale=[[0, "#fff9f9"], [1, "#2cb94f"]],
                zmin=0,
                zmax=1,
                marker_opacity=0.35,
                marker_line_width=0.3,
                showscale=False,
                hovertemplate="County FIPS: %{location}<br>Has data: Yes<extra></extra>"
            )
        ],
        frames=frames
    )
        
    # Map styling and playback controls
    title_text = f"{table_name}: {value_col} by county and year"
    fig = mu.apply_map_layout_and_controls(fig, title_text, years)

    return fig

plot_county_coverage(df, "Air Quality", "county coverage")
```

Starting in 2020 there are a collection of counties that stop being representing in our dataset. They are not showing up as NA values for the years beyond 2020, they simply stop having entried for that county all together. County id 35003 in New Mexico is a good example of this issue. 

I double checked if this data existed right after loading in the raw data in the cleaning script to rule out bugs in the cleaning code. There is data for every day of 2019 for county 35003 but none for the same county in 2020. 

Use the following filtering logic to verrify this after loading in the raw data:
df_raw[(df_raw["year"]==2020) & (df_raw["statefips"] == "35") & (df_raw["countyfips"]=="3")]

#### Values by County

```{python}
# create a choropleth map of counties for a set of desired variables in the df

# Update these:
eda_table_name = "Air Quality"
cols_to_use = [15,19]

## one map per column
for i in cols_to_use:
    value_col = cols[i]
    map_df = df[["year", "county_id", value_col]].dropna()

    ## Get unique years
    years = sorted(map_df["year"].dropna().unique())

    frames = []

    value_min = map_df[value_col].min()
    value_max = map_df[value_col].max()


    frames = []
    for year in years:
        df_year = map_df[map_df["year"] == year] # dropped .copy() for speed
        
        frames.append(
            go.Frame(
                data=[
                    go.Choroplethmap(
                        locations=df_year["county_id"],
                        z=df_year[value_col]
                    )
                ],
                name=str(int(year))
            )
        )

    if not frames:
        raise ValueError(f"No valid yearly data found for {value_col}")

    initial_year_df = map_df[map_df["year"] == years[0]]

    fig = go.Figure(
        data=[
            go.Choroplethmap(
                geojson=counties_geojson, 
                locations=initial_year_df["county_id"],
                z=initial_year_df[value_col],
                featureidkey="id",
                colorscale="Viridis",
                zmin=value_min,
                zmax=value_max,
                marker_opacity=0.5,
                marker_line_width=0.3,
                colorbar=dict(title=value_col),
                hovertemplate=f"County FIPS: %{{location}}<br>{value_col}: %{{z}}<extra></extra>"
            )
        ],
        frames=frames
    )
        
    ## Make it look nice
    title_text = f"{eda_table_name}: {value_col} by county and year"
    fig = mu.apply_map_layout_and_controls(fig, title_text, years)

    fig.show()
```
